steps.prompt: Is the person struggling to speak in full sentences, turning blue around the lips, or showing no improvement after using their inhaler?

options.label: Mild to moderate attack — can still speak

steps.prompt: Call emergency services immediately. This is a severe attack. Sit the person upright — do not lay them down. If they have a reliever inhaler (blue/salbutamol), help them use it every minute until help arrives.
steps.cta: Call emergency services — sit upright and use inhaler

steps.prompt: Sit the person upright in a comfortable position — leaning slightly forward can help. Loosen any tight clothing around the chest and neck. Stay calm and encourage slow breathing.
If they have a reliever inhaler (usually blue), help them use it: 1 puff every 30–60 seconds, up to 10 puffs. Use a spacer if available — it delivers the medicine more effectively.
After using the inhaler, is the person's breathing improving within 5–10 minutes?

options.label: No — no improvement or getting worse

steps.prompt: Call emergency services. Continue helping them use the inhaler every minute until help arrives. Do not leave them alone.
steps.cta: Call emergency services — continue inhaler every minute

steps.prompt: Even if improved, the person should see a doctor or go to hospital today. An asthma attack that needed this much reliever should always be medically reviewed.
